prompt: A photorealistic straight-on electronics maker-bench photo: three capacitors are wired in a MIXED network -- capacitor C1 is IN SERIES with a PARALLEL pair made of C2 and C3 (that is, C2 and C3 are wired in parallel with each other, and that pair is then in series with C1) -- and a bench CAPACITANCE / LCR meter set to microfarads is clipped across the whole network, its LCD reading the TOTAL capacitance. Each capacitor has its value printed on its body: C1 = 4.7 uF, C2 = 10 uF, C3 = 22 uF. Work the two rules in order: capacitors in PARALLEL ADD (so the C2 C3 pair equals C2 plus C3), then that pair is in SERIES with C1, where series capacitance is found from one over the total equals one over C1 plus one over the parallel pair. Compute that total and show it on the meter's LCD in microfarads, as a clear number (two decimal places). Remember series and parallel capacitors combine by OPPOSITE rules; do NOT just add the three values. Crisp bench lighting, the three printed capacitor values and the meter's numeric readout all sharp and legible, no other numbers anywhere.
